stem: After interdisciplinary evaluation, a pancreas transplant candidate meets all eligibility criteria without outstanding conditions. How should the coordinator communicate the team's recommendation?

options.text: Inform the patient they met eligibility criteria and are approved as a candidate
Defer any communication until an organ offer is received
Tell the patient they are permanently ineligible without further discussion
Instruct the patient to self-register on the national waitlist without program involvement

explanation.rationale_correct: Evaluation outcome communication includes informing patients when they met eligibility criteria and are approved as a transplant candidate.

rationale_incorrect.B: Team recommendations are communicated at evaluation conclusion, not deferred until organ offer.
rationale_incorrect.C: Meeting eligibility criteria results in approval communication, not permanent ineligibility.
rationale_incorrect.D: Waitlist registration occurs through the transplant program after approval, not independent self-registration.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 3, Patient Education → §7. Selection criteria and evaluation outcome → c.i.
primary_anchor.quote_hint: met eligibility criteria and is approved as a candidate

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 3 → §7. Selection criteria and evaluation outcome → c.i. (approved as candidate); PDF p. 100 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. Third 020400 item; second pancreas organ tag; distinct from not-listed (cctc-2017) and conditional approval (cctc-2024); anchor verified on Cupples p. 100.

stem: A lung transplant candidate currently smokes cigarettes and requests immediate waitlist activation. What OPTN-aligned program requirement should the coordinator explain?

options.text: A period of smoking cessation before listing, confirmed by random urine cotinine testing
Active smoking has no effect on lung transplant listing
Cotinine testing is prohibited for all transplant candidates
Smoking cessation is required only after transplantation, not before listing

explanation.rationale_correct: Most transplant programs require a period of smoking cessation before listing patients who currently smoke or have recent smoking history, with cessation confirmed by random urine cotinine testing.

rationale_incorrect.B: Smoking history affects listing requirements and post-transplant outcomes in lung and other organ populations.
rationale_incorrect.C: Cotinine testing is used to confirm smoking cessation before listing.
rationale_incorrect.D: Smoking cessation is required before listing, not only after transplant.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 1, Consultations → J.2.d. smoking cessation before listing
primary_anchor.quote_hint: require a period of smoking cessation before listing … confirmed by random urine cotinine testing

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 1 → J. Consultations → 2. Pulmonary evaluation → d. (smoking cessation and cotinine testing before listing); PDF p. 33 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. Fifth lung organ item; waitlist maintenance angle distinct from LAS updates (cctc-2021); anchor verified on Cupples p. 33.

stem: While compiling a multidisciplinary evaluation plan for a waitlisted candidate, which support resources should the coordinator identify per standard waitlist management references?

options.text: Social worker, registered dietician, and financial coordinator
Only the transplant surgeon without ancillary services
Exclusive reliance on the patient's employer for all psychosocial needs
No caregiver or financial support resources because they are optional

explanation.rationale_correct: Transplant coordinator waitlist responsibilities include identifying patient and caregiver support resources such as social worker, registered dietician, financial coordinator, and support groups.

rationale_incorrect.B: Multidisciplinary evaluation and waitlist management include ancillary support services beyond surgery alone.
rationale_incorrect.C: Employers do not replace structured transplant program support resources.
rationale_incorrect.D: Support resources are explicitly identified as coordinator responsibilities during the waiting period.

stem: During pretransplant evaluation coordination for a heart transplant candidate, which baseline pulmonary studies are required for all patients referred for transplantation?

options.text: Chest radiograph and pulse oximetry oxygen saturation
No pulmonary assessment because heart candidates are exempt

explanation.rationale_correct: All patients referred for transplantation should have a chest radiograph and oxygen saturation evaluated by pulse oximetry as part of baseline pulmonary evaluation.

rationale_incorrect.B: LAS applies to lung allocation, not the universal baseline pulmonary studies for all transplant referrals.
rationale_incorrect.C: Heart and other organ candidates receive baseline pulmonary screening per consultation references.
rationale_incorrect.D: PELD is a pediatric liver allocation score, not the described universal pulmonary baseline.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 1, Consultations → J.2.a. pulmonary evaluation baseline
